The engine computes what relaxing one of *your own* asks would be worth and
hands you the number; it never takes the offer for you, because only you can
say truthfully that you are free on a Saturday.

**The count is real.** It comes from re-running the whole search at this
rung — not from an estimate, and not from the strict count plus something.

weight.title: Weight
weight.description: The **renormalised** weight — this term's share of a hundred over the terms that actually fired.

contribution.title: Contribution
contribution.description: The weight times the value. The contributions sum to the Fit.

ScoredTermSchema.title: ScoredTermSchema
ScoredTermSchema.description: One term that produced a reading, and what it was worth here.

search_id.title: Search Id
search_id.description: The answer's identity. Minted server-side and recorded before this response was returned.

mode.description: Null exactly on the deck, which has no mode.

index_stale.title: Index Stale
index_stale.description: Whether the candidate index was more than fifteen minutes behind the log. The search was served either way; past a day it would have been refused instead.

radius_clamp.title: Radius Clamp
radius_clamp.description: Whether a widening offer hit the profile slider's own ceiling. False on a search that widened nothing.

sorts_available.title: Sorts Available
sorts_available.description: Which re-sorts the client may draw over rows it already holds. **A sort that would reorder nothing is not in this list**, and the control is not drawn — a visible control that does nothing is the product lying quietly. Re-sorting costs no round trip.

rung_offers.title: Rung Offers
rung_offers.description:
What relaxing your own asks would be worth, each with a real count from a genuine re-run.

**`null` means the offers were not computed at all** — your shortlist was long enough that nobody needed them. An empty list means they were computed and there is nothing left to offer, which is the honest empty state: the pool beside it is the whole answer.

prompts.title: Prompts
prompts.description: Questions this search raises, each of which changes nothing until you answer it. Present on a search and **omitted on a read-back**, where a month-old question would be asked about a value that has since moved.

SearchEnvelope.title: SearchEnvelope
SearchEnvelope.description:
Every fact about *the search*, as opposed to about a candidate.

One object, identical on every route that creates a search: one renderer, one
type.

SearchMode.title: SearchMode
SearchMode.description:
What kind of evening this search is for. **Two values, never three.**

``PlayIntent`` is the *candidate's* declaration and has three values;
``SearchMode`` is the *searcher's* setting — which tab they are on, right
now — and has two. ``app/modules/player_profile/domain/play_intent.py`` says
where this type belongs when it arrives: *"it belongs to the matcher and not
to this module"*. Here it is.

**There is never a ``NO_PREFERENCE`` weight vector.** A candidate who
declared ``NO_PREFERENCE`` is indifferent about the kind of evening, so their
reverse fit runs under the *searcher's* mode: ``NO_PREFERENCE`` never selects
a weight vector, it inherits one (``ranking-weights.md`` §9). The arities
differ on purpose, so the likeliest bug in the matcher is a type error rather
than a paragraph in a document.

minimum_km.title: Minimum Km
minimum_km.description: Smallest radius a player may hold

maximum_km.title: Maximum Km
maximum_km.description: Largest radius a player may hold

SearchRadiusBoundsResource.title: SearchRadiusBoundsResource
SearchRadiusBoundsResource.description:
The range a Search radius may take, in whole kilometres.

The unit is in every field name on purpose: a bare ``minimum`` is one
refactor away from being read as metres.

SearchSurface.title: SearchSurface
SearchSurface.description:
Which terminal stage ran. Four values, and pooling their rates is how
every number the engine is judged by becomes meaningless — ``FILL_SEATS`` is
not even optimising for the searcher.

``SHORTLIST`` and ``DECK`` can be written today; the two line-up surfaces
arrive with their route. All four were declared before any of them could be
written, because ``surface`` is a stored column and a vocabulary that grows
one value per ticket is a vocabulary whose old rows cannot be read against
the new ones.

day.title: Day
day.description: ISO weekday — 1 is Monday, 7 is Sunday. The grid is Monday-first.

SharedSlot.title: SharedSlot
SharedSlot.description:
The next cell of the week both players ticked.

**The grid is never rendered to anybody as a calendar.** Only the count of
shared slots and the name of the next shared one are ever shown, because
overlap is a fact about a pair where a calendar is a fact about a person.

candidates.title: Candidates
candidates.description:
Ranked. **An empty list is a `200`** — the honest empty state is an answer, not a failure.

A read-back may carry withheld rows: the record is immutable and the gates are live, so a row the product has since agreed not to show keeps its place and states that it is withheld. Branch on `withheld` — a fresh search never carries one.

ShortlistResponse.title: ShortlistResponse
ShortlistResponse.description:
The whole answer: one envelope, and at most twenty rows.

**Bounded and unpaginated.** There is no page two; past the last row there
are rung offers or an honest empty state. The bound is ruleset data, so a
client never reads twenty from anywhere — it renders the rows it is given.

Side.title: Side
Side.description: Which side of the net. The searcher is always on ``A``.

SidesSchema.title: SidesSchema
SidesSchema.description:
The two sides of the net. **You are always on `A`.**

There is no arrangement in which the searcher crosses the net, because
*which side am I on* is not a question a builder asks: what varies is who is
beside you.

SocialTag.title: SocialTag
SocialTag.description: The closed set of tag ids. An id here is permanent.

SocialTagGroup.title: SocialTagGroup
SocialTagGroup.description: The three groups, which are about the game and nothing else.

SocialTagGroupResource.title: SocialTagGroupResource
SocialTagGroupResource.description: One of the three groups, with its tags in the order they are rendered.

SocialTagResource.title: SocialTagResource
SocialTagResource.description:
One tag, as an id and nothing else — for now.

An object rather than a bare string deliberately: retiring a tag is
anticipated (an id is honoured forever and hidden from the picker), and a
tag that carries a field one day is an addition here, where an array of
strings would have to change element type — which breaks a shipped client.

minimum_tags.title: Minimum Tags
minimum_tags.description: Fewest tags a player may hold — the picker's floor

maximum_tags.title: Maximum Tags
maximum_tags.description: Most tags a player may hold — the picker's ceiling

SocialTagSelectionBoundsResource.title: SocialTagSelectionBoundsResource
SocialTagSelectionBoundsResource.description:
How many Social tags a selection must hold to be one.

The unit is in both field names for the reason it is on the radius bounds:
a bare ``minimum`` beside a list of eighteen tags reads as a count of
something, and which something is exactly what a client would guess wrong.

matched.title: Matched
matched.description: Tag ids they both hold, in this column

SocialVibeEvidence.title: SocialVibeEvidence
SocialVibeEvidence.description:
What the two of them are like around the game.

The same shape as playing style and deliberately a **separate variant**: the
two terms carry different weights, invert between the modes, and a client
renders them under different headings. One variant with a column field would
make *which term is this* a value the client has to branch on rather than a
type it can dispatch over.

SortOption.title: SortOption
SortOption.description:
The re-sorts a client may offer over rows it already holds.

**Server-driven, and a sort that would reorder nothing is not drawn.** A
client deriving offerability from ``degraded_terms`` would be encoding a
sort-to-term mapping, which is the objection that promoted ``distance_km``
out of the distance evidence in the first place.

``MOST_RELIABLE`` is in the vocabulary and is never offered today: the
reliability term stands down for everybody, so the control **is not drawn**
rather than drawn and inert.

Sport.title: Sport
Sport.description: The four sports Raketa rates, as a closed enum.

players.title: Players
players.description: Number of players the sport is played for

SportResource.title: SportResource
SportResource.description: One sport as served: how many play it and the durations it is sold in.

StrandReading.title: StrandReading
StrandReading.description:
One reliability strand that produced a reading.

A strand with too few observations **stands down and is absent from the
list** rather than present at zero: *we have not seen enough* and *they are
bad at this* are different facts, and a term may never be honestly neutral.

TagPair.title: TagPair
TagPair.description:
Two tag ids one relationship row fired on.

Ids only. The row's kind is the field it sits under, its column is the term
it sits under, and its strength or severity is a ruleset number the player is
not shown — what is owed here is *which two things about you two this reads*.

Term.title: Term
Term.description:
The eight terms of Fit, weighted per mode and renormalised per comparison.

Eight and not seven: the prototype's single ``vibe`` merges what the split
below keeps apart, and intent alignment is the term the prototype never had.
**The split between playing style and social vibe is by *relationship*, not
by tag group** — every matrix row carries its own column
(``ranking-weights.md`` §1).

Day one **reliability stands down** and the live seven renormalise; that is
the basis every judged reading and the quality floor were computed on.

TranscriptEntryResponse.title: TranscriptEntryResponse
TranscriptEntryResponse.description: One answered question: the question as it was asked, and what was chosen.

UncertaintyFactorResponse.title: UncertaintyFactorResponse
UncertaintyFactorResponse.description: Something that widened the range instead of moving the estimate.

UnfilledReason.title: UnfilledReason
UnfilledReason.description:
Why a seat is empty, and why the four-way week is.

``the-group-objective.md`` §5.1's closed vocabulary. **A partial line-up is
always a `200`**: *three of four* is an honest answer, and *nobody* is the
same shape with three seats carrying a reason rather than a separate empty
state.

``NO_ADMISSIBLE_COMBINATION`` is the one ``docs/adr/0116`` added and it is
load-bearing: without it a six-pair gate is indistinguishable from a thin
pool, on the screen and in the telemetry — and after
``docs/adr/0113`` it is also how a screen says *nobody at their level yet*
about a newcomer's first four rather than *nobody*.

adult_attested.title: Adult Attested
adult_attested.description: The player's own claim that they are an adult. Required, and required to be `true`: the platform is adults only and that is a precondition of holding an account. `false` is refused with `adult_attestation_required`, and the client writes the sentence. **Not a date of birth and not age verification** — this records that the question was asked and answered, and nothing more.

has_player_profile.title: Has Player Profile
has_player_profile.description: Whether this player has committed a Player profile — the fourth branch of the entry gate. Read from the profile's own event stream rather than from a projection, so it is correct immediately after the commit that creates one. False on a response that is not about the authenticated player, such as the one registration returns.

UserResponse.title: UserResponse
UserResponse.description:
The account, plus the one fact about it onboarding's entry gate needs.

``has_player_profile`` is not a property of a ``User`` and the domain layer
has no idea it exists — it is answered by the Player profile context and
joined here, on the response, because the gate reads it on every cold launch
and a second round trip for one boolean would be a second thing to fail
(``docs/adr/0090``).

**It is not an "onboarded" flag.** The rating context's invariant against one
stands: whether a player has been through onboarding *for a sport* is asked
by asking whether a rating exists for that sport, and this field cannot
answer it. This asks a genuinely per-player question, because a profile is
one per player and has no sport dimension at all.

Window.title: Window
Window.description:
When a game found on a grid would plausibly be played. **A code, never a
sentence** — *"tonight"* is the client's word (``docs/adr/0022``).

**Derived, never chosen** (``docs/adr/0100``). There is no window picker
anywhere: a player changes their window by changing their grid, which is the
same act that changes their matches. One control, one meaning.

It is a **label on the search**, not a proposed time — the grid is still
never rendered to anybody as a calendar, and this says only how soon the week
it ran on comes round.

WireInclusionReason.title: WireInclusionReason
WireInclusionReason.description:
Why this person is in the list at all — **and it is a union of one.**

The store keeps three values and the wire publishes this one, which is the
whole of ``the-two-contracts.md`` §4's *the store is open where the wire is
closed*. Only an **interest lift** admits anybody; the other two **reorder**,
and a reorder is not a reason a searcher is owed:

- ``NEWCOMER_WINDOW`` reaches the client as a Liveness reason instead, which
  is where a printable reorder belongs.
- ``ZERO_EXPOSURE`` never crosses at all. *You are seeing this person because
  nobody has been shown them all week* is a third party's unpopularity, and
  the searcher is owed no version of it.

It stays an enum of one rather than a bare literal so the next reason that
genuinely **admits** somebody has somewhere to go.

withheld.title: Withheld
withheld.description: Always `true`. This row was recorded and is no longer shown: the fail-closed gates were re-evaluated at read time and one of them excludes it now. **Which one is deliberately not said.**

WithheldRowSchema.title: WithheldRowSchema
WithheldRowSchema.description:
A row that was recorded, and that the live gates no longer admit.

**Stated, never vanished.** A read-back that quietly returned nineteen rows
where twenty were recorded is the same class of lie as a breakdown that
quietly stops adding up, and worse for being invisible — so the row keeps its
place in the list and says what happened to it.

**It names no gate, and it carries no person.** The four fail-closed gates
are a block either way, a hold, an account that may not be shown, and the
mutual gender preference; naming which one fired would tell a searcher that a
particular person blocked them, was suspended, or changed a safety setting.
``docs/adr/0095`` is explicit that *neither party is ever notified and the
other side sees no trace anywhere in any response*, and that rule does not
weaken because the surface has a longer memory. So this shape has one field,
